451271.long_answer: Diltiazem is a non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that has been used off-label to treat calcinosis cutis by modulating calcium deposition in tissues. It is supported by case reports, which suggest that it may help reduce calcium accumulation in the skin.

269763.long_answer: Individuals with Acrorenal mandibular syndrome may exhibit fibular aplasia. The fibula, located on the lateral side of the tibia, is the bone that is absent in this condition, according to established skeletal anomaly descriptions associated with the syndrome.

497392.long_answer: Craniofrontonasal dysplasia is an X-linked dominant osteochondrodysplasia that causes unique craniofacial abnormalities. Mutations in the EFNB1 gene disrupt normal cell signaling during development, leading to the characteristic facial dysmorphisms observed in affected individuals.

644924.long_answer: The FLT1 gene, which encodes both the membrane-bound and soluble forms (sFLT1) of VEGF receptor-1, is located on human Chromosome 13. The upregulation of the sFLT1 isoform is strongly implicated in the pathogenesis of pre-eclampsia, a significant hypertensive disorder of pregnancy.

572211.long_answer: In the repair of interrupted aortic arch, an essential step is the ligation (tying off) of the patent ductus arteriosus. This procedure prevents the abnormal blood flow through the ductus, thereby allowing the surgeon to reconstruct the aortic arch, typically via an end‐to‐end anastomosis. The ligation of the ductus is a critical component in stabilizing circulation in infants before or during definitive aortic repair.

909300.long_answer: Tufted angioma is a benign vascular tumor that is known to sometimes present with a mild thrombocytopenia as part of the Kasabach–Merritt phenomenon. This condition involves localized platelet trapping by the vascular tumor, and although the phenomenon is also seen in kaposiform hemangioendothelioma, tufted angioma is characteristically associated with a milder form of thrombocytopenia.

238297.long_answer: The thalamus is a central relay station that integrates and modulates motor and sensory signals. In juvenile myoclonic epilepsy, abnormal thalamocortical network dynamics, involving the thalamus, are consistently observed, linking it to the motor control disruptions and myoclonic jerks characteristic of this disorder.

187627.long_answer: The plaque reduction neutralization test (PRNT) is the gold standard diagnostic test for arbovirus infections. It definitively identifies specific virus-neutralizing antibodies, reducing cross-reactivity and providing conclusive evidence of infection.

716904.long_answer: Autosomal dominant nanophthalmos has been linked to mutations in the TMEM98 gene, which is located on human chromosome 17. This association is well-established in literature, pinpointing the genetic basis for the condition.

419335.long_answer: Fetal Alcohol Syndrome is a developmental disorder resulting from prenatal alcohol exposure that can impair fine motor skills among other neurodevelopmental and physical abnormalities. The disorder is characterized by facial dysmorphology, growth deficiencies, and central nervous system dysfunction.

925706.long_answer: Lemons and limes are high in vitamin C and were historically used to prevent and treat scurvy. During the Age of Sail, British naval practices, informed by early studies such as those by James Lind, utilized these citrus fruits to counter vitamin C deficiency, thereby reducing the incidence of scurvy among sailors.

736446.long_answer: Ureteral reimplantation is the surgical treatment used to prevent reflux in patients with megaureter. This procedure involves repositioning the ureter into the bladder with the creation of a submucosal tunnel, which acts as a functional valve to prevent the backflow of urine into the ureter.

556481.long_answer: The limb malformations seen in ectrodactyly‐polydactyly syndrome have been most clearly linked to alterations in a critical region on chromosome 7q21. In many affected individuals a microdeletion in this region—encompassing the DLX5 and DLX6 genes—is responsible for the abnormal limb development. These genes play key roles in limb patterning and morphogenesis during embryogenesis, and their haploinsufficiency disrupts normal digital formation.

630221.long_answer: There is no well‐documented or widely reported evidence in the scientific or journalistic record that any New York Times columnist has been identified as having coloboma—a congenital ocular defect. No reputable biographical or medical source confirms that any such columnist has this condition.

802889.long_answer: Mismatch repair cancer syndrome typically refers to conditions characterized by deficiencies in the mismatch repair system that predispose individuals to cancer, most notably Lynch syndrome. Lynch syndrome is recognized as the most common hereditary colorectal cancer syndrome, with an estimated prevalence of around 1 in 300 to 1 in 500 individuals in many populations. This relatively high prevalence among inherited cancer syndromes means that it is not considered a rare disease. It is important to note that while another related condition, constitutional mismatch repair deficiency syndrome (CMMRD), is indeed a rare autosomal recessive disorder, the term 'mismatch repair cancer syndrome' is more commonly associated with Lynch syndrome and similar conditions, which are not rare.

599273.long_answer: The NS3 protease, in complex with its cofactor NS2B, cleaves the polyprotein of the West Nile virus into individual functional proteins. This proteolytic processing is crucial for viral replication and the formation of mature viral components.

298495.long_answer: Tachycardia, or an increased heart rate, is commonly seen in patients with right atrial enlargement due to the strain and potential arrhythmias associated with the enlarged atrium. It is also a well-recognized component of the body’s anti‐infection defense mechanism, as fever and other inflammatory responses often lead to a compensatory increase in heart rate.

118956.long_answer: Duplicated opposable triphalangeal thumbs are most frequently associated with point mutations in the Zone of Polarizing Activity Regulatory Sequence (ZRS), a long-range enhancer located in an intron of the LMBR1 gene. This mutation alters Sonic Hedgehog (SHH) expression during limb development, leading to the triphalangeal thumb phenotype.

383891.long_answer: The National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) has updated its guidelines for the management of desmoid tumors, now favoring active surveillance rather than immediate surgical resection as the first-line treatment due to the high recurrence rates and potential surgical morbidity associated with these tumors.

140177.long_answer: Myeloid leukemia is indeed classified as a hematologic disease. It is a type of cancer that arises from the myeloid line of blood cells, which are part of the hematopoietic system. This classification is supported by established biomedical consensus that categorizes leukemia, including myeloid variants, as malignancies affecting blood-forming tissues.

473145.long_answer: Extended mouth opening during dental procedures—especially those requiring prolonged periods of immobility such as extractions or extensive restorative work—can place strain on the temporomandibular joint, potentially leading to joint dysfunction characterized by pain, inflammation, and reduced mobility.

518647.long_answer: The primary treatment for encephaloceles is surgical repair. This involves resecting nonfunctional brain tissue if necessary and closing the skull defect to prevent complications and secure the brain's normal structure.

826630.long_answer: Basophils are a type of granulocyte that play a role in the inflammatory response by releasing histamine, which increases capillary permeability and facilitates the migration of other immune cells to sites of infection.

182412.long_answer: The mediastinum is the central compartment of the thoracic cavity housing vital organs such as the heart and esophagus, and it is commonly affected in cases of lymphoma, particularly subtypes like primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma.

579743.long_answer: Pineoblastoma is a type of primitive neuroectodermal tumor that is associated with retinoblastoma, particularly in the context of trilateral retinoblastoma, where individuals with retinoblastoma develop an intracranial tumor in the pineal region.

237160.long_answer: The genetic condition causing split hand/split foot malformation (SHFM) associated with a duplication on chromosome 10q24 typically follows an autosomal dominant pattern. In this inheritance mode, a single copy of the mutated gene is sufficient to cause the condition, which exhibits variable expressivity.

148648.long_answer: Duplications on the short arm (Xp) of the X chromosome have been linked to X-linked intellectual disability. These duplications involve alterations in gene dosage that can disrupt normal neurodevelopment, a finding that is well supported by genomic studies of affected individuals.

320415.long_answer: Androgen therapy, such as treatment with oxymetholone, is used as a temporary measure to stimulate bone marrow hematopoiesis in Fanconi anemia patients. This approach can help improve blood counts until definitive treatment, like hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, can be implemented.

779776.long_answer: Human Herpesvirus 6, particularly the HHV-6B variant, is known to cause encephalitis in transplant recipients. In immunocompromised patients, such as those receiving hematopoietic stem cell transplants, reactivation of latent HHV-6 can lead to limbic encephalitis, presenting with symptoms like fever, altered mental status, and seizures.

496487.long_answer: Tandem mass spectrometry is the technique used in newborn screening to detect an abnormal acylcarnitine profile, which indicates systemic primary carnitine deficiency. By analyzing the levels of carnitine and acylcarnitines, this method allows early identification and intervention.

717411.long_answer: Conversion disorder was reclassified as part of functional neurological disorder (FND), a term that encompasses a range of conditions characterized by neurological symptoms—including movement problems—that are not explained by underlying structural or neurodegenerative pathology. This reclassification reflects a better integration of neurobiological and psychological mechanisms underlying these symptoms.

247687.long_answer: The X-linked form of Fanconi anemia is caused by mutations in the FANCB gene. Unlike the autosomal recessive forms of Fanconi anemia, which are caused by mutations in various other FANCA, FANCC, and other related genes, the FANCB gene is located on the X chromosome and is responsible for the X-linked phenotype observed in affected individuals.

544392.long_answer: Gout is an inflammatory arthritis caused by the deposition of monosodium urate crystals in joints due to hyperuricemia (high blood uric acid levels). This condition is commonly associated with aortic stenosis, especially in patients with overlapping cardiovascular risk factors.

363296.long_answer: The family with Upington disease originated in the Northern Cape province of South Africa, which is where the town of Upington is located.

295599.long_answer: Familial dysbetalipoproteinemia is most commonly associated with the homozygous ApoE2 genotype. This mutation in the ApoE gene impairs the clearance of chylomicron and VLDL remnants, leading to their accumulation and subsequent increased risk of atherosclerosis.

236305.long_answer: Cyclosporine is an immunosuppressive agent that inhibits T-cell activation. It is used to prevent organ transplant rejection and has also been utilized in the treatment of immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP), particularly in cases that are refractory to first-line therapies.

800151.long_answer: Hyperprolinemia, which involves elevated levels of proline in the blood due to enzymatic defects in proline metabolism, is inherited in an autosomal recessive manner. This means that an affected individual must inherit two mutated copies of the relevant gene, one from each parent, to manifest the condition.

600052.long_answer: WAGR syndrome is caused by a deletion on chromosome 11, which includes the WT1 gene that is critical for normal genitourinary development. Disruption of WT1 leads to the genitourinary anomalies seen in this condition.

901445.long_answer: Cysteine is crucial for the structural stability of many extracellular domains through disulfide bond formation. In the usherin protein, which is linked to Usher syndrome type II, conserved cysteine residues within EGF‐like or laminin globular domains are essential for proper folding and function. These regions are vital for the development and maintenance of the inner ear and retina, and mutations affecting cysteine residues can disrupt protein structure, thereby contributing to the pathology of Usher syndrome type II.

177946.long_answer: Isodisomy is a form of uniparental disomy in which an individual inherits two identical copies of a chromosome from one parent. This can unmask autosomal recessive mutations, leading to the manifestation of rare recessive disorders.

714068.long_answer: Pediculosis corporis is an infestation of the body louse (Pediculus humanus corporis) that typically occurs in settings of poor hygiene and malnutrition. These conditions favor louse proliferation and can lead to widespread skin irritation, excoriations, and secondary bacterial infections.

406891.long_answer: During the convalescent stage of whooping cough, the patient gradually recovers from the severe symptoms experienced in earlier stages, although they can still be contagious. This phase typically features a reduction in the frequency and severity of coughing spells, along with a slow return to normal respiratory health.

295842.long_answer: Anagen effluvium is a condition characterized by the sudden loss of actively growing hair. This disorder is commonly seen after exposure to toxins — such as chemotherapeutic agents or heavy metals like arsenic or thallium — which also cause systemic poisoning effects. Due to the rapid onset of hair loss and accompanying systemic signs, anagen effluvium can be mistaken for poisoning.

639671.long_answer: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) inhibit cyclooxygenase enzymes, reducing prostaglandin synthesis which is essential for maintaining the protective gastrointestinal mucosal barrier. Their use increases the risk of upper gastrointestinal bleeding, making them particularly concerning for patients with Mallory-Weiss syndrome.

787973.long_answer: Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE) is a progressive neurological disorder that, among other symptoms, leads to motor abnormalities including increased muscle tone, which is the hallmark of spasticity. Both conditions are characterized by hypertonicity, resulting in muscle stiffness and exaggerated reflexes due to upper motor neuron involvement.

734252.long_answer: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is commonly used to demonstrate brain atrophy, including decreased sizes of the cerebellum and pons in patients with multiple system atrophy.

708868.long_answer: Proteus-like syndrome is a rare overgrowth disorder caused by mosaic mutations, typically involving the AKT1 gene. Medical geneticists are best equipped to diagnose this condition using genetic testing and clinical criteria, and they coordinate multidisciplinary care for its complex manifestations.

458719.long_answer: Lithium toxicity primarily affects the principal cells in the collecting duct. Lithium enters these cells via epithelial sodium channels (ENaC) and disrupts the action of vasopressin, impairing water reabsorption and leading to nephrogenic diabetes insipidus.

969723.long_answer: Roberts syndrome is caused by mutations in the ESCO2 gene, which is located on human chromosome 17. This gene plays a crucial role in establishing sister chromatid cohesion during cell division, and its disruption leads to the characteristic developmental defects observed in Roberts syndrome.

923758.long_answer: Ataxia–telangiectasia is caused by mutations in the ATM gene, which encodes a key kinase in the DNA damage response. Moreover, ATM phosphorylates aprataxin—the protein mutated in ataxia–ocular apraxia-1—establishing a functional link between these two disorders.

236850.long_answer: Corticosteroids are endogenous hormones produced in the adrenal cortex and are used exogenously as anti-inflammatory drugs, including in the treatment of birdshot chorioretinopathy to reduce immune-mediated inflammation.

922123.long_answer: Vitamin B12 deficiency is known to cause peripheral neuropathy by impairing the production of myelin, which is essential for nerve function. This deficiency can lead to demyelination and nerve damage, manifesting as tingling, numbness, and pain in the extremities.

682809.long_answer: LIG4 syndrome is caused by mutations in the LIG4 gene, which is crucial for the non-homologous end joining pathway of DNA double-strand break repair. This condition is associated with microcephaly, immunodeficiency, and developmental delay due to impaired DNA repair mechanisms.

711731.long_answer: The gene associated with Type II focal facial dermal dysplasia, TWIST2, is located on human chromosome 2. Mutations in TWIST2 cause Setleis syndrome—a form of this dysplasia—confirming the chromosomal location.

144206.long_answer: Research into dinosaur paleopathologies has documented unusual bony outgrowths, or exostoses, on the tail vertebrae of a psittacosaurid species. Psittacosaurus, a basal ceratopsian known from Early Cretaceous deposits in Asia, includes a species in which such vertebral exostosis was observed—an abnormality likely resulting from trauma or local pathological processes. This finding adds to the understanding of injury and healing in non‐avian dinosaurs.

246638.long_answer: Woodhouse–Sakati syndrome is caused by mutations in the DCAF17 gene, which encodes a protein involved in various cellular mechanisms. Gene duplication analysis can identify copy number alterations in this gene, aiding in the diagnosis of the syndrome.

361826.long_answer: Nijmegen breakage syndrome is caused by mutations in the NBN gene, which is located on the long arm of human chromosome 8 (specifically 8q21).

112466.long_answer: Transbronchial lung biopsy is a procedure performed during bronchoscopy to obtain small samples of lung tissue. These samples are examined histologically to identify noncaseating granulomas, which are characteristic of berylliosis, thereby confirming the diagnosis.

218245.long_answer: Sodium bicarbonate is used to treat metabolic acidosis in patients with glutathione synthetase deficiency. It acts as an alkalinizing agent that neutralizes excess acid in the blood, thereby helping to restore acid-base balance.

717088.long_answer: Mutations in the MYH3 gene, which encodes the embryonic myosin heavy chain, are known to cause Freeman-Sheldon syndrome (a type of distal arthrogryposis). This syndrome is characterized by congenital contractures—including those of the hands and feet—and distinctive facial features. In some cases, patients may also present with cleft palate, thereby linking the MYH3 mutation to this specific form of arthrogryposis.

782231.long_answer: The proposal linking Joseph Merrick, known as the Elephant Man, to Proteus syndrome was published in an article in the British Medical Journal. This publication examined Merrick’s clinical characteristics in light of what is known about Proteus syndrome, thereby initiating the discussion and subsequent debate over his diagnosis.

378548.long_answer: Meningococcal septicemia is a severe bloodstream infection caused by Neisseria meningitidis. Even with prompt and aggressive treatment, it carries a significant risk, with mortality rates around 10-15% or higher in some cases. The outcome depends largely on early diagnosis and rapid initiation of therapy, with delays resulting in an increased risk of shock, disseminated intravascular coagulation, and multisystem failure. Survivors may also face long-term complications.

264134.long_answer: Maple Syrup Urine Disease is caused by a deficiency in the branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase complex, leading to the accumulation of branched-chain amino acids and their toxic byproducts, which can result in ketoacidosis.

133342.long_answer: The hypothalamus contributes to PCOS development through dysregulation of the GnRH pulse generator. Altered pulse frequency increases luteinizing hormone (LH) relative to follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), leading to enhanced ovarian androgen production, disrupted follicular development, and the characteristic hormonal imbalance seen in PCOS.

922144.long_answer: Tetrasomy 9p involves an isochromosome for the short arm of chromosome 9, and one of the recognized markers is the increased dosage of genes mapped there. The ALDOB gene, which encodes the enzyme aldolase B and is located at 9p13.3, is used as a biochemical marker. Measuring aldolase B activity can help in the diagnosis of tetrasomy 9p by detecting its elevated levels resulting from the extra copies of the gene.

988272.long_answer: Pediatric dermatologists are specialists in skin disorders in newborns and children. Osteoma cutis, characterized by the formation of bone within the skin, is treated primarily through dermatological management, making pediatric dermatology the most appropriate specialty for a newborn with this condition.

709278.long_answer: DNAH5 encodes an axonemal dynein heavy chain essential for the proper function of motile cilia. Mutations in DNAH5 are a frequent cause of primary ciliary dyskinesia. Recent studies have also implicated DNAH5 in modulating the epithelial response and mucociliary clearance in the nasal passages, playing a role in the inflammatory processes observed in allergic rhinitis.

783517.long_answer: Volar soft tissue release is a surgical technique used to correct wrist flexion contractures in children with amyoplasia-type arthrogryposis. The procedure involves releasing the contracted ligaments, joint capsules, and tendinous tissues on the volar (anterior) aspect of the wrist, thereby allowing improved extension and better function.

156824.long_answer: Finnish-type PEHO syndrome is a severe neurodegenerative disorder characterized by rapid neurological decline, refractory seizures, and multisystem involvement, leading to a poor prognosis with death typically occurring in early childhood.

515811.long_answer: Excessive androgen production in females can lead to virilization, which involves the development of male secondary sexual characteristics such as a deepened voice, increased body hair, and clitoromegaly.

767594.long_answer: In individuals with XX gonadal dysgenesis, the development of pubic hair is attributed to adrenal androgens, particularly dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA), which are produced by the adrenal cortex. These androgens stimulate secondary sexual hair development independent of ovarian estrogen production.

582943.long_answer: Molluscum contagiosum causes lesions that are raised, pink, and feature a central dimple. These are clinically described as umbilicated papules, which is a hallmark sign of this poxvirus infection.

615395.long_answer: The basal lamina, a component of the alveolar basement membrane, functions as a structural scaffold that facilitates fibroblast migration and organization following epithelial injury. This supports the development of intraluminal fibroblast plugs characteristic of cryptogenic organizing pneumonia.

864306.long_answer: The disease commonly known as Leprechaunism, or Donohue syndrome, is caused by mutations in the insulin receptor gene (INSR). The INSR gene is located on Chromosome 19, making it the specific chromosomal locus responsible for this genetic disorder.

292697.long_answer: Lewy body dementia is known to feature dysautonomia as a symptom. The presence of alpha-synuclein pathology in both cortical and autonomic brainstem regions can lead to autonomic dysfunction, manifesting as orthostatic hypotension, urinary incontinence, and other dysautonomic symptoms.

703637.long_answer: Arakawa’s syndrome II is classified as a mitochondrial disorder—a type of inborn error of metabolism that stems from defects in mitochondrial function, which in turn impairs cellular energy production. This categorization is based on established scientific consensus on disorders that directly affect mitochondrial metabolic pathways.

128090.long_answer: Kounis syndrome involves an acute coronary syndrome triggered by an allergic reaction, resulting in myocardial ischemia. Cardiologists are the specialists who diagnose and treat the heart-related aspects of the condition, including managing coronary vasospasm and myocardial infarction.

569989.long_answer: Cohen syndrome is a genetic disorder caused by mutations in the VPS13B gene. This syndrome is characterized by developmental delay, intellectual disability, microcephaly, as well as various neurological manifestations that can include seizures.

201042.long_answer: The measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine is recommended because it contains the attenuated rubella virus, which protects against rubella infection. Preventing rubella in women of childbearing age is crucial to avoid congenital rubella syndrome in newborns.

923861.long_answer: The diagnosis of collagenous colitis is confirmed by obtaining a colonic mucosal biopsy. Histological examination of the biopsy, often with the use of special stains such as Masson trichrome, reveals the thickened subepithelial collagen layer characteristic of the disease.

733954.long_answer: Most Turbellaria species exhibit simultaneous hermaphroditism, meaning that individual organisms have both male and female reproductive organs concurrently. This reproductive strategy allows them to exchange sperm during copulation, enhancing their reproductive success.

786504.long_answer: Autosomal dominant centronuclear myopathy is primarily associated with mutations in the DNM2 gene, which is located on chromosome 19. DNM2 encodes the protein dynamin 2, which is essential for membrane trafficking and cytoskeletal dynamics.

466064.long_answer: Tyrosinemia, particularly type I, is associated with an autosomal recessive inheritance pattern. This means that an individual must inherit two copies of the mutated gene (one from each parent) to exhibit the disease.

973485.long_answer: Cyclosporine is an immunosuppressive drug that is used in the treatment of birdshot chorioretinopathy and is also widely employed to prevent organ transplant rejection. It works by inhibiting T-lymphocyte activation, thereby reducing inflammation and immune-mediated damage.

708783.long_answer: Motile cilia, with their characteristic 9+2 microtubule arrangement, are present on the epithelial cells of the fallopian tubes. In endosalpingiosis, similar ciliated cells are found ectopically, supporting the role of motile cilia in salpingoitic tissue growth outside the fallopian tubes.

585147.long_answer: Mutations in the TCOF1 gene are most frequently associated with Treacher Collins syndrome, a craniofacial disorder that affects the development of facial bones and ears, often resulting in hearing loss due to malformations in the structures of the ear.

461462.long_answer: The cytochrome bc1 complex contains two b-type hemes (referred to as heme bL and heme bH) in its cytochrome b subunit. These hemes are essential for the electron transfer process in the Q-cycle, making the b-type heme a defining component of the complex.

700204.long_answer: The MYOC (myocilin) gene mutation is primarily linked to primary open-angle glaucoma, not primary congenital glaucoma. Primary congenital glaucoma is more commonly associated with mutations in the CYP1B1 gene and sometimes the LTBP2 gene. Thus, based on established scientific consensus, there is no widely recognized connection between MYOC mutations and primary congenital glaucoma.

110825.long_answer: Gum arabic, also known as acacia gum, is a natural exudate used as an emulsifier in pharmaceuticals and food products. Occupational exposure to airborne particles of gum arabic in manufacturing settings has been documented to induce asthma in sensitized individuals.

637196.long_answer: A Double-J stent is a specialized ureteral stent designed to ensure proper urine drainage from the kidney to the bladder. It is used in cases such as a dilated ureter (megaureter) to relieve obstruction and maintain urinary flow, thereby protecting kidney function.

892903.long_answer: Mepolizumab is an anti-IL-5 monoclonal antibody that targets eosinophils by inhibiting interleukin-5, thereby reducing eosinophil production and activity. It is used in the treatment of hypereosinophilic syndrome to control eosinophilia and its associated symptoms.

872766.long_answer: Rapid ascent in scuba diving can lead to lung barotrauma that causes alveolar rupture, allowing air to enter the bloodstream. This air can then be forced into the arterial circulation, leading to an arterial gas embolism, which is a serious and potentially life-threatening complication.

968541.long_answer: Cystic hygroma is the outdated term historically used to describe what is now classified as lymphatic malformations. Advances in imaging and genetic studies have refined the classification and understanding of these lesions, leading to the preference for the term lymphatic malformations in modern medical research and clinical practice.

312129.long_answer: Jarcho-Levin syndrome is a congenital disorder characterized by abnormalities in the spine and ribs. Because these musculoskeletal deformities primarily affect children, patients are typically managed by pediatric orthopedic specialists.

131248.long_answer: Jalili syndrome is an autosomal recessive condition caused by mutations in the CNNM4 gene, leading to compound heterozygosity. This condition is characterized by cone-rod dystrophy and amelogenesis imperfecta, affecting both vision and dental enamel formation.

525704.long_answer: In mucopolysaccharidosis, glycosaminoglycan deposition can lead to bony and soft tissue abnormalities that result in spinal cord compression, most notably in the cervical region, ultimately causing cervical myelopathy.

195909.long_answer: Mast cells are the primary immune cells involved in type I hypersensitivity reactions. They become activated when their surface-bound IgE antibodies encounter specific allergens, leading to degranulation and the release of various mediators such as histamine, which cause the allergic symptoms.

390297.long_answer: Petroleum jelly, commonly known as petrolatum, is an occlusive moisturizer that helps retain skin hydration, making it effective in the treatment of psoriasis. It is also a frequent ingredient in baby lotions and cosmetics due to its gentle and hydrating properties.

980245.long_answer: Radiology is a leading journal in the field of diagnostic imaging that publishes articles covering a wide range of topics including the radiologic diagnosis of rare conditions like eosinophilic fasciitis. Its focus on advanced imaging techniques makes it an appropriate venue for such studies.

342020.long_answer: The gene associated with cerebellar ataxia in Boucher-Neuhäuser syndrome is PNPLA6, which is located on chromosome 19, specifically in the 19p13.2 region. This gene plays a critical role in neuronal function, and its mutation is well-documented in this syndrome.

671155.long_answer: Tympanostomy tubes, commonly known as grommets, are sometimes used to treat hearing loss in individuals with primary ciliary dyskinesia. These devices are inserted into the tympanic membrane to help equalize pressure and drain fluid from the middle ear, mitigating conductive hearing loss associated with chronic otitis media.

580599.long_answer: Restless legs syndrome (RLS) is a neurological disorder that can lead to disrupted sleep and subsequent hypersomnia. It is well-established that iron deficiency is a significant contributing factor to RLS, likely due to its impact on dopamine metabolism, which plays a key role in the disorder's pathophysiology.

889115.long_answer: Low-density lipoprotein (LDL) is widely recognized as a significant risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular diseases because it transports cholesterol to the arterial walls, where it can accumulate and form plaque that narrows and hardens arteries.

255159.long_answer: Abu al-Qasim al-Zahrawi, also known by his Latinized name Albucasis, was a prominent Andalusian surgeon whose extensive writings in the field of surgery are well recognized. He is credited with first describing syndactyly as a congenital malformation, contributing foundational knowledge to the study of birth anomalies.

530744.long_answer: Feingold syndrome type 1 is caused by mutations in the MYCN gene, which is located on chromosome 2 (specifically at 2p24.1).

941721.long_answer: In individuals with complete trisomy 9, one of the characteristic skeletal anomalies is a shortened femur. Prenatal and postnatal evaluations have consistently demonstrated that the femur, one of the major long bones, tends to be unusually short relative to gestational age, making it an important marker in the description of the syndrome.

462115.long_answer: Infliximab is a TNF-α inhibitor commonly used in the treatment of autoimmune conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis, Crohn’s disease, and ulcerative colitis. Although there are isolated case reports of its use in refractory microscopic colitis (which includes collagenous colitis), infliximab is not an established or standard treatment for collagenous colitis. The recommended first‐line treatment for collagenous colitis is typically budesonide, and current clinical guidelines do not endorse routine infliximab use for this condition. Therefore, based on established biomedical consensus, infliximab is not generally used to treat collagenous colitis.

209032.long_answer: Performance appraisal is a systematic evaluation of an employee's work performance that can expose individuals with ergophobia to stress, criticism, and anxiety. Such evaluations often emphasize shortcomings or create pressure, potentially worsening the fear of work characteristic of ergophobia.

174838.long_answer: Amniocentesis is a prenatal diagnostic procedure in which a sample of amniotic fluid is collected to analyze fetal cells. These cells can be subjected to genetic testing, enabling the detection of mutations in genes (such as LIS1 or DCX) linked to lissencephaly. It is widely used to diagnose genetic conditions before birth.

284076.long_answer: Branchio-oto-renal syndrome is most commonly associated with mutations in the EYA1 gene, which is located on human chromosome 8 (specifically at 8q13.3). This gene plays a crucial role in the development of the ear, branchial arches, and kidneys, and its alteration leads to the characteristic features of the syndrome.

616645.long_answer: The endocardial cushions are critical structures in the developing heart that contribute to the formation of the atrial and ventricular septa as well as the atrioventricular valves. Abnormal development or remodeling of the endocardial cushions can lead to congenital heart defects, including atrial and ventricular septal defects.

253624.long_answer: Gardner's syndrome is a variant of familial adenomatous polyposis, which results from mutations in the APC gene. The APC gene is located on chromosome 5, specifically on the long arm (5q21).

561535.long_answer: Zinc oxide is a physical sunscreen agent that reflects and scatters UVA and UVB light. This broad-spectrum protection helps reduce photosensitivity reactions in conditions like Gunther disease (congenital erythropoietic porphyria), where patients are particularly vulnerable to UV-induced damage.

663330.long_answer: Papulopustular rosacea is the subtype characterized by edematous papules and pustules along with central facial erythema. This presentation typically involves inflammatory lesions that may be mistaken for acne, but it is a distinct inflammatory dermatosis associated with rosacea.

489470.long_answer: Spinocerebellar ataxia-14 (SCA14) is associated with mutations in the PRKCG gene, which is located on human chromosome 19.

550846.long_answer: Both dysexecutive syndrome and dementia typically involve problems with executive functions, which include planning, decision-making, problem-solving, and cognitive flexibility. Impaired executive functioning is a core feature in the clinical presentation of these conditions.

529790.long_answer: Barth syndrome is an X-linked mitochondrial disorder characterized by defects in cardiolipin remodeling. This defect typically leads to cardiac complications, most notably dilated cardiomyopathy, which is the heart condition commonly associated with the syndrome.

498376.long_answer: Patients with 6-Pyruvoyltetrahydropterin synthase deficiency already have compromised tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) production, which is essential for the synthesis of neurotransmitters and proper amino acid metabolism. Methotrexate, as a folate antagonist, inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, which further interferes with folate and BH4 metabolism. This additional disruption can worsen the BH4 deficiency, leading to aggravated metabolic and neurological complications.

277960.long_answer: Diabetes can lead to higher blood sugar levels that promote the growth of Candida species, making patients more susceptible to candidiasis. This fungal infection, commonly caused by Candida albicans, often manifests as oral thrush or skin infections and is well-documented among individuals with diabetes.

614237.long_answer: Finnish-type PEHO syndrome has been associated with mutations in the ZNHIT3 gene. This gene mutation is linked to a neurodegenerative condition that causes severe epileptic seizures along with other neurological manifestations.

379103.long_answer: Midface hypoplasia is a common craniofacial abnormality seen in syndromic craniosynostosis, where the midface does not develop properly. This underdevelopment can lead to a narrowed upper airway, significantly increasing the risk of obstructive sleep apnea.

661221.long_answer: Mutations in the PDGFB gene are linked to Primary familial brain calcification. PDGFB encodes the platelet‐derived growth factor B, which is critical for maintaining vascular integrity, including the regulation of tight junctions between high endothelial cells.

559437.long_answer: Antihistamines are used to treat the pruritus (itching) associated with Schamberg's disease by blocking histamine receptors, which helps reduce the itch sensation and alleviate discomfort.

727325.long_answer: Mutations in the SPAST gene, which encodes the microtubule-severing protein spastin, are responsible for approximately 25% of inherited cases of spastic paraplegia. These mutations impair normal axonal function, leading to degeneration of the corticospinal tract.

769307.long_answer: Acute pancreatitis is an inflammatory condition of the pancreas that can lead to symptoms such as vomiting, severe abdominal pain, and nausea. It is commonly associated with gallstones and heavy alcohol consumption.

852122.long_answer: Esotropia, characterized by inward turning of the eye, is most commonly addressed in children by specialists in pediatric ophthalmology. This medical specialty focuses on eye disorders in the pediatric population, including strabismus, making them best equipped to manage and treat conditions like esotropia.

443226.long_answer: Refsum disease is most commonly associated with mutations in the PHYH gene, which encodes the enzyme phytanoyl-CoA hydroxylase. This enzyme is crucial for the alpha-oxidation of phytanic acid. When mutated, phytanic acid accumulates, contributing to several clinical features including hyperkeratosis.

818978.long_answer: Mowat–Wilson syndrome is caused by heterozygous mutations in the ZEB2 gene. Mutations in ZEB2 affect the development of multiple organ systems, and gastrointestinal issues, such as constipation in infants, are among the clinical features associated with this syndrome.

142532.long_answer: Cross syndrome was first characterized in 1971. That year marks the initial formal description in the biomedical literature that recognized the syndrome as a distinct clinical entity.

987874.long_answer: Elevated levels of Immunoglobulin A (IgA) are a well-recognized immunological feature in individuals with ankylosing spondylitis, reflecting increased mucosal immune system activity and linking the gut and joint inflammation observed in the disease.

498756.long_answer: ACE inhibitors are recommended as the first-line treatment for hypertension in patients with polycystic kidney disease. They help lower blood pressure, reduce proteinuria, and may slow kidney disease progression through their effects on the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system.

773749.long_answer: SLC20A2 encodes the phosphate transporter PiT-2 and is the gene most commonly associated with primary familial brain calcification. Although individual genes are not directly visualized by electron microscopy, the calcified deposits that result from SLC20A2 mutations can be examined at the ultrastructural level using this technique, linking its pathology to observable electron microscopic features.

805824.long_answer: California has banned the use of lindane for treating scabies due to its neurotoxic effects and environmental concerns. This measure reflects state-level regulatory efforts to prevent adverse health outcomes associated with the application of lindane.

668624.long_answer: Activated charcoal is typically administered via a nasogastric tube, particularly in cases of overdose such as with tricyclic antidepressants. This procedure ensures that the charcoal is delivered safely into the stomach for decontamination, especially when the patient is unable to take medications orally.

305802.long_answer: Phenytoin is an anticonvulsant used in the treatment of epilepsy. Its use during pregnancy has been linked to fetal hydantoin syndrome, which is characterized by a range of congenital anomalies due to in utero exposure.

808576.long_answer: Pneumocystis pneumonia, caused by the yeast-like fungus Pneumocystis jirovecii, is a well-established opportunistic infection that primarily affects individuals with compromised immune systems, such as those with AIDS or undergoing immunosuppressive therapies.

591650.long_answer: Ablative treatment with a carbon dioxide (CO2) laser has been reported as the most effective option for acrokeratoelastoidosis. This procedure vaporizes the superficial hyperkeratotic lesions, leading to significant cosmetic improvement with controlled tissue removal and low recurrence.

436007.long_answer: Cerebral cavernous malformations are most commonly found in the cerebral cortex. When these malformed vascular clusters compress cortical tissue, they can disrupt normal electrical activity, leading to dangerous seizures.

284260.long_answer: In primary myelofibrosis, neoplastic megakaryocytes produce cytokines such as TGF-beta, which stimulate resident bone marrow fibroblasts to secrete collagen and reticulin proteins, leading to the fibrotic changes seen in the disease.

813404.long_answer: The Mediterranean diet, which emphasizes fruits, vegetables, whole grains, lean proteins, and healthy fats like olive oil, has been shown to reduce the risk of type 2 diabetes by improving insulin sensitivity, reducing inflammation, and supporting weight management.

811818.long_answer: Vitreous floaters, also known by their Latin term muscae volitantes, occur when small particles or clumps within the vitreous humor cast shadows on the retina. This can lead to disturbances in the visual field, and is a well-recognized ocular condition.

402982.long_answer: Glossophobia, or the fear of public speaking, is a common manifestation of Social Anxiety Disorder. This disorder is characterized by an intense fear of social situations where one might be judged or scrutinized, leading to significant distress and avoidance behaviors, particularly in settings such as public speaking.

969999.long_answer: Rosenthal–Kloepfer syndrome is a rare condition with a likely genetic etiology that manifests as a complex, multi‐system finding. Clinical geneticists are specially trained in diagnosing and managing congenital and inherited disorders. They coordinate care with other specialties as needed, making clinical genetics the primary specialty for treatment of this syndrome.

300450.long_answer: GM1 gangliosidosis is a lysosomal storage disorder that typically presents in infancy or early childhood with progressive neurodegenerative symptoms. Pediatric neurologists specialize in managing such neurologic and metabolic conditions in children, making them key in diagnosing and treating this disorder.

117707.long_answer: Familial lecithin cholesterol acyltransferase deficiency alters lipid composition in red blood cell membranes, increasing their fragility and leading to accelerated hemolysis, which manifests as hemolytic anemia.

115743.long_answer: Cranial gliomas in patients with Ollier disease are associated with somatic mutations in the IDH1 gene. These mutations change the enzyme's function, leading to accumulation of the oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate, which is implicated in tumorigenesis.

716179.long_answer: Renal duplex ultrasound is a non-invasive imaging technique that utilizes Doppler flow measurements to assess blood flow velocities in the renal arteries, helping to identify stenotic lesions. It is commonly employed based on clinical prediction rules to screen for and evaluate the severity of renal artery stenosis.

276923.long_answer: Studies indicate that, in community samples, reactive attachment disorder (RAD) is estimated to affect about 1% of children. Rates may be higher among children with histories of severe neglect, maltreatment, or institutional care, but in the general population, the prevalence typically approximates 1%.

259012.long_answer: Acro-oto-radial syndrome is inherited in an autosomal recessive fashion. In populations where consanguinity (mating between close relatives) is common, there is an increased likelihood for rare, recessive mutations to become homozygous, thereby raising the incidence of such conditions.

360300.long_answer: Leukocyte Adhesion Deficiency Type II (LAD-II) is caused by mutations in the SLC35C1 gene, which encodes the GDP-fucose transporter. This gene is located on chromosome 11, and defects in its function lead to impaired fucosylation of glycoproteins, a key issue in LAD-II.

433180.long_answer: The CPS1 gene, which is responsible for carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I deficiency, is located on chromosome 2. This gene is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern, meaning it is carried on a non-sex (autosomal) chromosome rather than a sex chromosome.

723427.long_answer: The sympathetic nervous system triggers the release of catecholamines from the adrenal medulla. Under normal conditions, cortisol from the adrenal cortex induces the enzyme phenylethanolamine N-methyltransferase (PNMT) which converts norepinephrine to epinephrine. In adrenal insufficiency, reduced cortisol levels lead to diminished PNMT activity, resulting in impaired epinephrine synthesis and a weakened sympathetic stress response.

130588.long_answer: Long-term toluene exposure is primarily associated with neurotoxic effects in the cerebellum. Exposure leads to cerebellar degeneration, notably affecting Purkinje cells, which results in impaired motor coordination and balance.

602748.long_answer: Irene Maumenee was a pioneering ophthalmologist known for her work in ocular genetics. She was among the first to characterize the optic nerve colobomas that are seen in renal‐coloboma syndrome, an inherited condition caused by mutations in the PAX2 gene. Her detailed clinical characterization of these ocular anomalies has significantly contributed to our understanding of the syndrome.

936702.long_answer: Hymenolepiasis is a parasitic infection caused by the tapeworm Hymenolepis nana, which commonly affects children. Pediatric Infectious Diseases specialists are trained to diagnose and treat parasitic and other infectious diseases in children.

852311.long_answer: Congenital amelia is a genetic condition in which one or more limbs fail to form during development. Because these individuals grow up without an entire limb, they develop and depend on the proprioceptive input from their remaining limb structures and body schema. This entrenched proprioceptive mapping can lead to a preference for relying on the innate feedback mechanisms of their existing anatomy rather than transitioning to prosthetic devices, which generally provide less integrated proprioceptive information.

798619.long_answer: Folic acid supplementation is commonly used in managing hemoglobinopathies such as hemoglobin C disease. It helps support increased red blood cell production, which can improve anemia symptoms in affected individuals.

706701.long_answer: Pregabalin is commonly used to treat peripheral neuropathy and is known to cause fatigue among its side effects. It acts by modulating calcium channels, which can lead to sedative and fatigue-related effects in patients.

363581.long_answer: The ICD-10 code for hepatorenal syndrome is K76.7. This classification is used to identify the clinical condition where advanced liver disease leads to kidney failure.

522090.long_answer: Systemic corticosteroids, such as oral prednisone, are considered the gold standard treatment for Sweet syndrome. These drugs rapidly reduce the inflammatory response and neutrophilic infiltration, which are hallmarks of the condition, leading to significant improvement in clinical symptoms.

674865.long_answer: TIPS (transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt) was found to be more effective at removing ascites compared to paracentesis in a meta-analysis. TIPS works by reducing portal hypertension, which is a primary contributor to the development of ascites in patients, thus offering a more definitive management strategy than repeated paracentesis.

177009.long_answer: Acute viral illnesses can trigger a metabolic crisis in individuals with short-chain acyl-coenzyme A dehydrogenase deficiency. The increased energy demand and catabolic stress during a viral infection can unmask the underlying defect in fatty acid oxidation, leading to the appearance of clinical symptoms.

812169.long_answer: Mutation in the LAMP2 gene causes Danon disease, an X-linked dominant disorder characterized by autophagic vacuolar myopathy, cardiomyopathy, and other systemic findings. The impaired function of LAMP2 disrupts lysosomal autophagy, leading to the accumulation of autophagic vacuoles in affected tissues.

188114.long_answer: Thyroid storm is a severe and life-threatening exacerbation of hyperthyroidism that can be precipitated by infections. It is characterized by extreme hypermetabolic symptoms such as high fever, tachycardia, and altered mental status, making it a medical emergency.

139363.long_answer: A hip–knee–ankle–foot orthosis (HKAFO) is an orthotic device specifically designed to provide comprehensive support to the legs and pelvis. It helps stabilize weakened muscles and improves mobility in patients with conditions like Becker muscular dystrophy by supporting the entire lower extremity during ambulation.

821690.long_answer: The gene responsible for 5α-Reductase 2 deficiency is SRD5A2, which is located on chromosome 2 (specifically at 2p23). Mutations in this gene disrupt normal conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone (DHT), leading to intersex traits.

144693.long_answer: Bronchogenic cysts typically contain a lining of ciliated respiratory epithelium accompanied by smooth muscle tissue in their walls, reflecting their origin from the foregut and bronchial tree structures.

147680.long_answer: Distraction osteogenesis is a surgical technique used to gradually lengthen bones. In cases of brachydactyly, it can be applied to the phalanges to improve digital function by stimulating new bone growth and increasing digit length.

801145.long_answer: The olfactory nerve, or cranial nerve I, is unique because its sensory neurons extend from the nasal epithelium into the brain. This direct connection provides a pathway by which bacteria—capable of causing severe sepsis, meningitis, or encephalitis—may gain access to the central nervous system.

190127.long_answer: Metachromatic leukodystrophy is a rare autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disorder caused by a deficiency of the enzyme arylsulfatase A. The incidence is generally estimated at approximately 1 in 40,000 births in the general population.

324885.long_answer: FLAIR (Fluid Attenuated Inversion Recovery) MRI is a technique that suppresses the high signal from cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), allowing for improved visualization of abnormalities adjacent to CSF spaces. In the context of diagnosing ALS, this method can help reveal subtle pathological changes, especially in the corticospinal tracts.

583694.long_answer: Goldenhar syndrome is typically considered to have a multifactorial inheritance pattern, where both genetic predisposition and environmental factors contribute to the phenotype. This explains why familial clustering can be observed even though most cases are sporadic.

719555.long_answer: Both Turner syndrome and Noonan syndrome are classically associated with a webbed neck that extends to the shoulders. Turner syndrome, occurring in females with a missing or partially missing X chromosome, is well-known for this physical feature, while Noonan syndrome, which can affect both males and females, presents with similar phenotypic characteristics including a webbed neck.

385631.long_answer: Herpes simplex virus, particularly HSV-1, is known to cause a dendritic pattern of inflammation and ulceration in the corneal epithelium, a hallmark of herpes simplex keratitis.

847439.long_answer: Pfam is a comprehensive database of protein families that includes curated alignments and hidden Markov models, making it an ideal resource for finding detailed information on families such as those containing cytochrome c oxidase subunits.

823703.long_answer: Pyruvate carboxylase is a mitochondrial enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of pyruvate to oxaloacetate. Mutations in the PC gene result in its deficiency, impairing gluconeogenesis and leading to lactic acidosis.

452908.long_answer: Langer mesomelic dysplasia is associated with mutations in the SHOX gene, which is located in the pseudoautosomal region of the human sex chromosomes. Alterations in SHOX affect skeletal development, particularly causing mesomelic shortening of the limbs.

456443.long_answer: Mutations in the TBC1D24 gene are known to cause DOORS syndrome, a condition characterized by progressive sensorineural hearing loss and onychodystrophy (nail dystrophy) along with additional features like osteodystrophy and seizures.

365959.long_answer: Clostridioides difficile colitis is a type of colitis characterized by the formation of pseudomembranes in the colon. It is caused by the overgrowth of C. difficile bacteria, which release toxins that damage the intestinal lining, leading to the formation of pseudomembranes that are seen during diagnostic evaluations.

864624.long_answer: The HELLS gene, also known as LSH, is located on human Chromosome 10. Mutations in this gene have been linked to Immunodeficiency–centromeric instability–facial anomalies (ICF) syndrome type 4, making Chromosome 10 the locus of clinical relevance for this condition.

329668.long_answer: Glycogen storage disease type Ib is caused by a deficiency in glucose-6-phosphate translocase. This enzyme defect impairs the transport of glucose-6-phosphate into the endoplasmic reticulum for conversion to glucose, leading to metabolic disturbances and is uniquely associated with chronic neutropenia and increased infection risk.

187672.long_answer: Hirschsprung’s disease accompanied by hypoplastic (underdeveloped) nails and minor dysmorphic features is alternatively known as Nail‐gut syndrome. This eponym highlights the dual involvement of the enteric nervous system – resulting in aganglionic megacolon – along with nail dysgenesis, and is recognized as a neurocristopathy with a distinct set of clinical findings.

215930.long_answer: Chorea-acanthocytosis follows an autosomal recessive inheritance pattern. This means that an individual must inherit two mutated copies of the gene (often VPS13A) to exhibit the disease, while carriers with one mutated copy typically do not show symptoms.

416761.long_answer: Metaphyseal dysostosis refers to the abnormal development of the metaphyses, which are the regions of long bones between the diaphysis (shaft) and the epiphysis (end). In individuals with Metaphyseal dysostosis-intellectual disability-conductive deafness syndrome, the dysostosis primarily affects these metaphyseal regions, leading to skeletal abnormalities.

698966.long_answer: Waterhouse–Friderichsen syndrome causes acute adrenal insufficiency due to hemorrhage of the adrenal glands, necessitating replacement of cortisol. This is typically achieved through glucocorticoid replacement therapy, often using hydrocortisone, to restore proper adrenal function.

324134.long_answer: Goldenhar syndrome is linked to developmental abnormalities in the first and second pharyngeal (branchial) arches. These embryonic structures contribute to the formation of facial features, ears, and parts of the eye, which explains many of the clinical manifestations seen in the syndrome.

223969.long_answer: Microcephalic primordial dwarfism, Montreal type is a rare congenital condition characterized by severe growth retardation and microcephaly. Pediatric geneticists specialize in diagnosing and managing rare genetic and developmental disorders in children, making them the most likely specialists to handle the diagnosis and treatment of this condition.

747817.long_answer: B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) is a hormone released from the ventricular myocardium in response to increased wall stress, making it a useful and widely accepted biomarker for diagnosing various forms of heart failure, including peripartum cardiomyopathy.

501533.long_answer: Haemochromatosis type 3 is caused by mutations in the TFR2 gene, and this gene is located on chromosome 7. The TFR2 gene plays a key role in iron homeostasis, and its mutation leads to altered iron regulation in the body.

151922.long_answer: Astaxanthin is a carotenoid pigment found in certain algae, notably Haematococcus pluvialis, which accumulates in animals such as flamingos and crustaceans, imparting a characteristic pink to red coloration. It is also used as a dietary supplement due to its potent antioxidant properties.

106128.long_answer: Nondisjunction is a meiotic error where homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids fail to separate properly, leading to gametes with an abnormal number of chromosomes. When such a gamete is involved in fertilization, and a trisomy is subsequently corrected (trisomy rescue), the removal of one chromosome can result in both remaining chromosomes being derived from the same parent, causing uniparental disomy.

932318.long_answer: The GH1 gene encodes growth hormone and is the most commonly implicated gene in familial isolated growth hormone deficiency. Variants in GH1 influence growth factor regulation, and alterations in growth hormone levels have been linked to soft tissue changes such as those observed in carpal tunnel syndrome. Thus, GH1 is the gene associated with both growth hormone deficiency and an increased risk of carpal tunnel syndrome.

180429.long_answer: This condition results from an immune reaction to a group A Streptococcus infection, commonly originating from untreated or partially treated acute tonsillitis. Immune complexes deposit in the kidney glomeruli, leading to inflammation and impaired kidney function.

829891.long_answer: A tissue (lesional) biopsy is the diagnostic procedure used to confirm chronic multifocal Langerhans cell histiocytosis. The biopsy typically reveals characteristic Langerhans cells, and immunohistochemical staining showing positive markers such as CD1a and langerin further confirms the diagnosis.

454005.long_answer: Epidemiological studies have shown that the autosomal dominant form of osteopetrosis appears at a higher frequency in Denmark compared to the United States. Genetic studies in Denmark have uncovered founder mutations that contribute to the relatively increased incidence of osteopetrosis in that population, whereas estimates in the U.S. (for instance, autosomal recessive osteopetrosis at roughly 1 in 250,000 births) indicate a lower overall rate.

628961.long_answer: Myoclonus dystonia is strongly associated with mutations in the SGCE gene, which encodes epsilon‐sarcoglycan, a transmembrane protein. Epsilon‐sarcoglycan is a component of the dystrophin‐glycoprotein complex located in the cell membrane, and its dysfunction disrupts normal signaling in neuronal and muscular tissues, contributing to the disorder’s pathology.

536999.long_answer: A cardiac myxoma is a benign neoplasm of the heart, most commonly originating from the endocardium. It is the most frequent primary cardiac tumor and consists of a gelatinous matrix produced by mesenchymal cells.

456454.long_answer: HOXD13 is a gene that resides on chromosome 2q31.1 and plays a key role in limb development. Mutations in or disruptions of this gene have been associated with brachydactyly type D, linking it to the abnormal development of the thumb.

676966.long_answer: Tracheoesophageal fistula is a congenital abnormality characterized by an abnormal connection between the esophagus and the trachea, typically resulting from an error in the separation of the foregut into the trachea and esophagus during embryonic development.

333727.long_answer: Zoe Sugg, widely known as Zoella, is a British social media personality who has publicly discussed her diagnosis of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). PCOS is a condition that, among other symptoms, can lead to hirsutism (excessive hair growth), irregular menstrual cycles, and acne. Her openness about the diagnosis has contributed to broader public awareness of the condition.

279203.long_answer: Yes, some medical journals have proposed that Joseph Merrick, known as the “Elephant Man,” might have suffered from Proteus syndrome. In the literature, this hypothesis emerged based on the range of his symptoms including asymmetric overgrowth, skin abnormalities, and bony deformities. While this proposal has been influential in discussions about his condition, it is important to note that the diagnosis remains controversial, with other theories (such as neurofibromatosis) also having been suggested. Nonetheless, the fact remains that at least a subset of the biomedical literature has indeed put forward Proteus syndrome as a possible explanation for Merrick’s clinical presentation.

158130.long_answer: Acute pancreatitis can lead to pancreatic endocrine insufficiency, resulting in diabetes mellitus (often referred to as type 3c or pancreatogenic diabetes). Diabetes has been identified as a risk factor for developing eating disorders such as bulimia nervosa due to complex metabolic, behavioral, and psychosocial associations.

533795.long_answer: Ceramic workers, particularly those involved in pottery and similar production processes, are at an increased risk for lung cancer due to prolonged exposure to respirable crystalline silica. This silica, present in clay and other ceramic materials, is a well-established carcinogen when inhaled over extended periods.

889195.long_answer: Hutchinson‐Gilford Progeria Syndrome (commonly known as progeria) features a very distinctive facial appearance with a narrow, aged face including a beaked nose, along with severe loss of subcutaneous fat and muscle wasting, which manifests as cachexia. This constellation of features is well established in the clinical description of the syndrome.

416985.long_answer: Perinatal asphyxia can trigger a stress state in newborns that leads to a transient form of congenital hyperinsulinism. This condition, often referred to as transient neonatal hyperinsulinism, is characterized by inappropriate insulin secretion in the immediate neonatal period, resulting in hypoglycemia.

130688.long_answer: Mutations in the DYNC2H1 gene, which encodes a component of the dynein motor complex involved in retrograde intraflagellar transport, are associated with Jeune asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy—a condition characterized by a narrow chest and small ribs.

137912.long_answer: In autoimmune hemolytic anemia, autoantibodies bind to red blood cells, marking them for destruction. Macrophages, particularly those in the spleen, recognize these opsonized cells via Fc receptors and phagocytose them, leading to hemolysis.

828462.long_answer: Todd's paralysis is a transient neurological deficit characterized by focal weakness or paralysis in part or all of the body following a seizure. It is a postictal phenomenon that typically resolves within hours to days.

602605.long_answer: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery, first published in 1899, is a classic surgical textbook that has long been used as an authoritative reference in clinical surgery. This textbook includes detailed information on the diagnosis and treatment of various surgical conditions, including compartment syndrome.

838281.long_answer: Mutations in TNFRSF11A, which encodes the receptor activator of nuclear factor-kappa B (RANK), have been identified in individuals with dysosteosclerosis. This gene is located on chromosome 18 and is essential for regulating osteoclast differentiation and bone remodeling, making its disruption a key factor in the disease.

425837.long_answer: Trisomy 16 is the most common chromosomal abnormality found in miscarriages. This condition, which involves an extra copy of chromosome 16, typically results in early developmental failure, leading to miscarriage.

703717.long_answer: Viljoen–Kallis–Voges syndrome is suspected to follow an autosomal dominant mode of inheritance, typically characterized by de novo variants. This pattern is consistent with many rare neurodevelopmental disorders where a mutation in a single copy of a gene leads to the condition.

359140.long_answer: Growth hormone therapy is used to stimulate growth in individuals with Aarskog–Scott syndrome, effectively improving growth velocity and addressing the short stature commonly associated with the condition.

995786.long_answer: Vacuolar myelopathy is a neurological disorder associated with HIV infection that often manifests as spastic paraparesis or motor dysfunction resembling paraplegia. It involves vacuolization and demyelination in the spinal cord's white matter, leading to impaired motor function.

107945.long_answer: Achondrogenesis type II, a perinatal lethal skeletal dysplasia often resulting in stillbirth, is most commonly associated with mutations in the COL2A1 gene. This gene encodes type II collagen, which is crucial for the proper development of cartilage and bone.

765490.long_answer: A CT scan is the preferred imaging technique for diagnosing neurocysticercosis by effectively detecting calcified cysts in the brain. Its high sensitivity to calcifications makes it particularly suitable for identifying these lesions.

801505.long_answer: The Visna-maedi virus is a retrovirus, specifically classified as a lentivirus. It causes chronic conditions in sheep, including progressive neurologic and respiratory diseases.

416430.long_answer: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune neuromuscular disorder that is generally rare. Its prevalence in the general population is estimated to be around 20 cases per 100,000 individuals, which aligns with established epidemiological studies.

960205.long_answer: Mutations in the GREB1L gene have been implicated in both bilateral and unilateral renal agenesis. Disruption of GREB1L, which plays a role in kidney development, can lead to deficient renal formation in utero, resulting in oligohydramnios and consequently Potter sequence.

277233.long_answer: Macroglobulinemia, particularly Waldenström macroglobulinemia, is a blood disorder characterized by the overproduction of IgM antibodies. This condition is primarily managed by hematologists, specialists in blood diseases and related malignancies.

497877.long_answer: A mutation in the PKD1 gene, located at 16p13.3 (a region encompassed within 16p13-p12), causes Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD). This disorder is characterized by the formation of numerous cysts in the kidneys, leading to abnormal kidney function and eventually kidney failure.

786477.long_answer: Pernicious anemia results from an autoimmune attack on the gastric parietal cells located in the stomach mucosa. These cells produce intrinsic factor, which is essential for the absorption of vitamin B12. Their destruction leads to a deficiency in intrinsic factor and, subsequently, vitamin B12 deficiency.

278468.long_answer: Aicardi syndrome, a rare neurodevelopmental disorder primarily affecting females, is characterized by callosal agenesis, infantile spasms, and ocular abnormalities. There have been documented reports of choroid plexus papilloma, a benign tumor of the choroid plexus, occurring in individuals with this syndrome.

940951.long_answer: Ellis-van Creveld syndrome is a genetic disorder characterized by short stature with abnormally short fingers and toes, often accompanied by congenital heart defects, most commonly atrial septal defects. The disorder is caused by mutations in the EVC or EVC2 genes, affecting ciliary function during development.

177623.long_answer: Hydrogen cyanide is a potent inhibitor of cellular respiration that works by binding to cytochrome c oxidase, thereby preventing the utilization of oxygen at the cellular level. Inhalation of hydrogen cyanide can rapidly lead to hypoxia, which often manifests as respiratory distress and may cause a temporary cessation of breathing (apnea) as the respiratory centers in the brain fail to function properly. This effect is consistent with the established toxicological profile of hydrogen cyanide, although without prompt intervention, the cessation of breathing can quickly lead to irreversible damage or death.

246059.long_answer: Klinefelter syndrome is associated with primary gonadal failure, where the testes do not produce sufficient testosterone despite elevated levels of gonadotropins (LH and FSH), thus leading to hypergonadotropic hypogonadism.

802537.long_answer: Multiple case reports and reviews on Pentasomy X indicate that affected females typically have a tall stature, with an average height about 2 standard deviations above the norm for females. This is a well-documented feature of the syndrome.

398937.long_answer: Bromocriptine is a dopamine receptor agonist that effectively lowers prolactin secretion in prolactin-secreting pituitary tumors (prolactinomas). By activating dopamine receptors in the pituitary, it reduces prolactin production and can lead to a decrease in tumor size, thus alleviating symptoms, including those related to hypopituitarism.

183995.long_answer: The optic nerve passes out of the eye through a perforation in the sclera, specifically at the region known as the lamina cribrosa, which is part of the scleral structure.

254394.long_answer: Gray matter heterotopia most commonly occurs in the periventricular region, particularly along the lateral ventricles. This condition results from a disruption in neuronal migration during brain development, leading to the presence of ectopic clusters of neurons near the ventricles.

881484.long_answer: Parkes Weber syndrome is associated with mutations in the RASA1 gene, which is located on human chromosome 5. This gene plays a critical role in vascular development, and its mutation can lead to the abnormal vascular proliferation seen in the syndrome.

348648.long_answer: The urinary bladder is the organ responsible for storing urine and it can be affected by endometriosis. Endometriosis can involve pelvic organs, including the bladder, where ectopic endometrial tissue may implant and cause pain and dysfunction.

208599.long_answer: Fucosidosis is a lysosomal storage disorder resulting from a deficiency in the enzyme Alpha-L-fucosidase. This enzyme normally degrades fucose-containing compounds, so its deficiency leads to the accumulation of fucose moieties, causing the disease's symptoms.

611996.long_answer: The primary treatment for a biliary fistula caused by bile duct obstruction is to relieve the obstruction. Endoscopic biliary drainage, commonly performed using ERCP with stenting, is used to decompress the biliary tree. This reduces intraductal pressure, allows bile to flow normally into the duodenum, and facilitates the healing of the fistula.

743911.long_answer: The founder effect explains the high prevalence of xeroderma pigmentosum in certain populations. It occurs when a small group with a specific genetic mutation forms a population, leading to a higher frequency of that mutation, and consequently a greater incidence of the disorder.

259908.long_answer: Tuberous sclerosis is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by mutations in the TSC1 gene located on chromosome 9. The condition leads to the formation of benign tumors (hamartomas) in multiple organs, and scoliosis is one of the skeletal manifestations associated with this disorder.

203025.long_answer: Oculodentodigital dysplasia is most commonly associated with mutations in the GJA1 gene, which encodes the gap junction protein connexin43. This mutation disrupts intercellular communication and is a well-established contributor to the clinical manifestations of the disorder, including syndactyly.

305369.long_answer: Uniparental disomy occurs when both copies of a chromosome, or a segment thereof, are inherited from one parent instead of one copy from each parent. This can result in recessive conditions like Donnai–Barrow syndrome if both copies of the gene carry a mutation.

275032.long_answer: Botulinum toxin type A injections are used to treat spasticity in conditions with symptoms similar to hereditary spastic paraplegia. By blocking the release of acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction, it reduces muscle overactivity and spasm.

583433.long_answer: Mutations in the CPS1 gene cause carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I deficiency, an autosomal recessive disorder that impairs the first step of the urea cycle. This defect leads to an inability to convert ammonia into urea, resulting in hyperammonemia.

563459.long_answer: De Barsy syndrome, a rare progeroid disorder with cutis laxa, has been linked to mutations in the ALDH18A1 gene. This gene encodes an enzyme involved in proline synthesis, and its impairment leads to defects in elastic fiber formation, which is a key factor in both De Barsy syndrome and cutis laxa.

123839.long_answer: Koro is a culture-bound syndrome characterized by an acute episode of anxiety where the individual fears that their genitals are retracting into the body. This condition is typically managed within the psychiatric field, where experts evaluate and treat psychological disorders and anxiety-related phenomena.

867870.long_answer: Deficiency of cystathionine beta-synthase is the most common cause of homocystinuria. This enzyme is critical for converting homocysteine into cystathionine, and its deficiency results in the accumulation of homocysteine, leading to the clinical manifestations associated with the disorder.

512744.long_answer: Methotrexate is a cornerstone treatment in rheumatoid arthritis due to its anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive properties. It is also used in low doses for lymphomatoid papulosis, offering therapeutic benefit by modulating abnormal cell proliferation in this cutaneous lymphoproliferative disorder.

491816.long_answer: Mutations in the TBX22 gene are associated with X‐linked cleft palate and ankyloglossia. TBX22 is a T-box transcription factor crucial for palatal development, and its mutation has been widely studied and documented in the scientific literature, including numerous PubMed-indexed publications.

567771.long_answer: Alopecia areata is an autoimmune condition primarily affecting hair, but it can also involve the nails. One of the most common nail abnormalities seen in alopecia areata is nail pitting, which involves the presence of small depressions on the nail surface.

461766.long_answer: Infantile hemangioma is the most common vascular tumor in babies. It is not considered a birth defect because it typically develops during the first weeks of life rather than being present at birth, and it generally undergoes a natural progression of growth followed by spontaneous involution.

547164.long_answer: A nebulizer is used to administer epinephrine in its aerosolized form for severe cases of croup. This device converts the liquid medication into a fine mist, allowing the patient to inhale it directly into the lungs, which helps to quickly reduce airway inflammation and relieve respiratory distress.

797678.long_answer: The most reliable and established evidence indicates that the gene responsible for severe intellectual disability‐progressive spastic diplegia syndrome is located on the X chromosome. This localization is consistent with many X‐linked neurodevelopmental disorders where mutations manifest as severe cognitive impairment along with motor dysfunction such as spastic diplegia.

692612.long_answer: The Q248H mutation in the ferroportin gene (SLC40A1) is associated with African iron overload. It alters iron export from cells, which can lead to iron accumulation in tissues. This mutation has also been noted to have implications in diabetes, where disrupted iron homeostasis can contribute to complications.

146316.long_answer: Mutations in the CLN3 gene, located on chromosome 16, cause juvenile neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis (Batten disease). The gene plays a crucial role in lysosomal function, and its dysfunction leads to the accumulation of autofluorescent lipopigments within neurons.

826886.long_answer: Schwartz–Jampel syndrome is associated with continuous muscle activity and myotonic symptoms, which can lead to muscle damage. This damage often causes the release of muscle enzymes, including creatine kinase, into the bloodstream, resulting in elevated creatine kinase levels.

800917.long_answer: The congenital defect known as a sternal cleft is most commonly treated via primary surgical repair, especially in infancy. Early surgical intervention helps ensure proper chest wall stability, protects underlying organs, and provides better cosmetic results.

857979.long_answer: Sotos syndrome is most commonly associated with mutations in the NSD1 gene. In Japan, over 50 percent of cases are due to microdeletions within this gene. This leads to haploinsufficiency of NSD1, resulting in the overgrowth and developmental delays characteristic of the syndrome.

269409.long_answer: The CYLD gene is located on chromosome 16, specifically in the region 16q12-13. Mutations in this gene lead to CYLD cutaneous syndrome, which can manifest as familial cylindromatosis, Brooke-Spiegler syndrome, or multiple familial trichoepithelioma.
